answer: A coastal authority buys one early-warning signal for each inlet during a spiral storm. Agents commit forecasts before a hidden set of buoy readings is released, and lock collateral in a vault. Payment is tied to measurable improvement in evacuation time, with one reward slot per place and hour; accounts submitting the same signal divide that slot. A Sybil operator gains nothing by multiplying names unless it finds new useful evidence and risks more collateral. Captured buoys or leaked readings could still distort the test, so independent sensors and public audits matter.
